note: Landing-page subset of the NeuroNexus glossary. Plain English, American spelling, no em dashes. The full glossary (frontend/src/glossary/glossary.json) should become the single source; until then keep both in step.

sol.short: A Mars day: 24 h 39 min 35 s, about 40 minutes longer than an Earth day.

active-sol.short: The sol the console is set to. Changing it updates dust, sunlight, thermal context, rover position and the walk decision together.

ls.short: Mars's season calendar: 0 degrees is northern spring, 90 summer, 180 autumn, 270 winter. Dust storms are most common from about 180 to 360.

tau.short: How much dust in the air dims sunlight. Clear sols sit near 0.3; the 2018 global storm pushed it above 4.

storm-2018.short: A dust event in mid 2018 that covered the whole planet and ended the Opportunity rover's mission.

mola.short: Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter on NASA's Mars Global Surveyor. It mapped the height of all of Mars, at about 463 m per pixel in the global grid.

hirise.short: High Resolution Imaging Science Experiment on NASA's Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, the sharpest camera orbiting Mars. Its terrain models reach about 1 m per pixel.

ctx.short: Context Camera on Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter. Its terrain models are about 20 m per pixel and cover far more ground than HiRISE.

dtm.short: Digital terrain model: a grid of ground heights built from stereo image pairs.

ladder.short: NeuroNexus uses the sharpest terrain available at each spot (HiRISE, then CTX, then MOLA) and labels which one it used.

eva.short: Extravehicular activity: time an astronaut spends outside the habitat in a spacesuit.

pnr.short: The farthest point you can reach and still walk back within the EVA time, keeping a reserve.

walk-back-margin.short: The spare time left after walking back if you turn around at the planned point.

planning-limit.short: A threshold you set to flag a route for review. It is not a certified safety limit; real limits would come from mission flight rules.

ground-truth.short: Real measurements used to check a model. Here: the drives Curiosity and Perseverance actually recorded on Mars.

imu-tilt.short: How far a rover leaned, measured by its onboard inertial measurement unit. Used here as ground truth for slope.

p90-ratio.short: The rover's 90th-percentile tilt divided by the map's 90th-percentile slope. 1.00 means the map matches the steep ground the rover felt.

ci95.short: The range the true value likely falls in, estimated by resampling the data 1,000 times.

out-of-sample.short: Tested on a site that was not used to tune the method. Jezero ran the same code with no changes.

candidate.short: One route the Route Designer proposes for a goal, such as lowest distance or lowest terrain risk. No AI draws the geometry.

pareto.short: No other candidate is better on every goal at once.

themis.short: Thermal Emission Imaging System on NASA's 2001 Mars Odyssey. Its infrared camera measures how warm the surface appears from orbit.

brightness-temp.short: The temperature a perfect emitter would need to give off the infrared light THEMIS measured. It tracks surface temperature but is not identical to it.

sim-3292.short: The Geologic Map of Mars (Tanaka and others, 2014): rock units by age and origin at 1:20,000,000 scale.

mars-2000.short: The standard Mars latitude and longitude system used by NASA and USGS maps.

mars-intelligence.short: The console's assistant. It answers from project data through tool calls and labels every answer as AI interpretation.

tool-call.short: The assistant looked a value up through an app function instead of guessing it.

source-tag.short: The label beside a value naming its evidence class and source. Tap it for the full ledger entry.

command-index.short: A searchable list of every console action. Open it with Ctrl or Cmd plus K.

radial-wheel.short: A circular menu of feature groups. Double right-click, press W, or long-press on touch.

modeled.short: Output of a physical model, such as the NASA Ames Mars Global Climate Model. Not a measurement.
